$comment: DELIBERATE DECISION, see docs/phase2/CORE_SITE_PROTECTION.md.
Neither the protected site nor a Research/Care feature: documentation and
verification tooling. Nothing under these prefixes is imported by the client
bundle, mounted by the Express app, or served to a visitor, so a change here
cannot redesign or behaviorally modify the main website. Allowing them is what
lets this protection gate exist in the repo without the gate rejecting itself.
NOTE THE SINGULAR/PLURAL TRAP: 'scripts/' (plural) is tooling and is allowed;
'script/' (singular) is the production BUILD (script/build.mjs, referenced by
package.json's build and render-build) and stays PROTECTED in protectedPaths.
DELIBERATE DECISION, see docs/phase2/CORE_SITE_PROTECTION.md.
Test files pass the gate but are always REPORTED, wherever they live, including
inside the Research and Care write zones.
Why they pass: a test is never bundled or served, so it cannot redesign or
behaviorally modify the website. Refusing them would fire on ordinary Research
work (origin/main's own persistent-cart change touches
server/release-control-plane.test.ts) and would push people to widen this
manifest, which is the one move that defeats the whole mechanism.
Why they are still reported: the repo rule 'do not lower existing safety or
regression gates to make a build pass' is exactly the risk a silent test edit
carries. Review must confirm each touched test was strengthened, not weakened.
This is also what covers server/core-site-protection.test.ts itself: it sits
beside server/release-control-plane.test.ts because that is the repo's existing
home for acceptance tests (vitest.config.ts includes server/**/*.test.ts, and
tsconfig.json excludes **/*.test.ts from `npm run check`), and it is admitted by
the same rule as every other test rather than by a special case for itself.
The ONLY protected files a Research or Care candidate may touch, and only for a
minimal integration seam or the exact hash-locked Omega typography change set.
Every edit here requires ALL of:
1. an exclusive lease on the file for the duration of the change,
2. the minimum possible diff (a registration line, not a refactor),
3. a focused regression test proving no unrelated behavior moved,
4. QA confirmation that the diff contains no unrelated change.
The gate PASSES a seam edit but REPORTS it, so review never sees one by accident.
